nodes.name: Authentication & Session
nodes.description: Form-login authentication for the bank app: Spring Security wiring, BCrypt password hashing, and the UserDetailsService that resolves an Account into an authenticated principal. Every route except /register is closed until a session exists.

nodes.name: Security Filter Chain
nodes.description: Declares the HttpSecurity rules: CSRF disabled, /register public, everything else authenticated, custom /login page with /dashboard as the fixed success target, and same-origin frame options.

nodes.name: User Details Resolution
nodes.description: AccountService implements UserDetailsService; loadUserByUsername rebuilds an Account principal from the persisted row and attaches a single hardcoded USER authority.

nodes.name: Password Hashing
nodes.description: BCryptPasswordEncoder bean shared by the AuthenticationManagerBuilder for verification and by registration for encoding new passwords; plaintext passwords are never stored.

nodes.name: Account Registration
nodes.description: Creates a new Account with a BCrypt-hashed password and a zero opening balance, rejecting duplicate usernames with a RuntimeException surfaced back onto the register form.

nodes.name: Logout & Session Invalidation
nodes.description: Logout handler bound to /logout that invalidates the HTTP session, clears the SecurityContext, and redirects to /login?logout; linked from the navbar of every authenticated page.

nodes.name: Money Movement
nodes.description: The core banking behaviour: deposits, withdrawals, and account-to-account transfers. All balance mutations go through AccountService and each one writes a matching Transaction ledger row.

nodes.name: Deposit
nodes.description: Adds the requested BigDecimal to the account balance, saves the account, then records a "Deposit" transaction. No upper bound or amount validation is applied.

nodes.name: Withdrawal
nodes.description: Subtracts funds after an insufficient-funds guard, saves the account, and records a "Withdrawal" transaction; failures bubble up as RuntimeException and re-render the dashboard with an error.

nodes.name: Transfer Execution
nodes.description: Debits the sender, credits the recipient looked up by username, and writes two mirrored ledger rows ("Transfer Out to X" / "Transfer In from Y"). The method is not annotated @Transactional, so the four saves are not atomic.

nodes.name: Balance Guards & Error Surfacing
nodes.description: Insufficient-funds and unknown-recipient checks expressed as BigDecimal comparisons plus RuntimeException throws, caught in the controller and rendered into the dashboard's error paragraph.

nodes.name: Domain Model
nodes.description: The two JPA entities that make up the banking domain — Account (also the security principal) and Transaction (the append-only ledger row) — plus the one-to-many association between them.

nodes.name: Account Entity
nodes.description: @Entity with identity-generated id, username, BCrypt password, BigDecimal balance, and a @Transient authorities collection — it doubles as the Spring Security UserDetails implementation.

nodes.name: Transaction Entity
nodes.description: Ledger row holding amount, a free-text type string ("Deposit", "Withdrawal", "Transfer Out to …"), a LocalDateTime timestamp, and a @ManyToOne back-reference to the owning account.

nodes.name: Entity Associations
nodes.description: Account owns a @OneToMany(mappedBy = "account") list of transactions while Transaction carries the account_id join column, making transactions the owning side of the relationship.

nodes.name: Account & Transaction Persistence
nodes.description: Spring Data JPA repositories over MySQL, with Hibernate generating and updating the schema at startup. All reads and writes in the app funnel through these two interfaces.

nodes.name: Account Repository
nodes.description: JpaRepository<Account, Long> with the derived finder findByUsername, which backs both authentication and every username-addressed operation such as transfer recipient lookup.

nodes.name: Transaction Repository
nodes.description: JpaRepository<Transaction, Long> exposing findByAccountId, the single query that materialises a user's statement.

nodes.name: Schema Management
nodes.description: Schema is derived from the entities by Hibernate (ddl-auto=update, MySQL8Dialect, show-sql on) rather than by migrations; the bundled SQL script placeholder is the only checked-in DDL artefact.

nodes.name: MySQL Datasource
nodes.description: JDBC coordinates for the bankappdb MySQL instance, including the credentials baked into application.properties and the runtime MySQL Connector/J dependency declared in the POM.

nodes.name: Transaction History
nodes.description: The read-only statement path: fetch every ledger row for the signed-in account and render it as a credit/debit coloured table.

nodes.name: History Query
nodes.description: getTransactionHistory resolves the account id and delegates to TransactionRepository.findByAccountId; there is no paging, sorting, or date filtering.

nodes.name: Ledger Labelling
nodes.description: Transaction type strings are composed at write time ("Transfer Out to <user>") and re-parsed at render time to decide credit vs debit styling — the sign of a movement is inferred from text, not stored.

nodes.name: Statement View
nodes.description: Thymeleaf table iterating ${transactions}, colouring amounts green for deposits and inbound transfers and red otherwise, with a link back to the dashboard.

nodes.name: Web Request Routing
nodes.description: BankController is the single Spring MVC entry point: eight handlers mapping the browser's GET pages and POST form submissions onto AccountService calls, with the current user pulled from the SecurityContext on every request.

nodes.name: Dashboard Route
nodes.description: GET /dashboard resolves the principal's account and puts it on the model as ${account} for the balance panel and the three money-movement forms.

nodes.name: Money Movement Routes
nodes.description: POST /deposit, /withdraw, and /transfer accept BigDecimal amounts as request params and redirect back to /dashboard on success, re-rendering the dashboard with an error attribute on failure.

nodes.name: Login & Registration Routes
nodes.description: GET /login and GET /register serve the two unauthenticated pages; POST /register creates the account and redirects to the login page. POST /login is handled by Spring Security's filter, not the controller.

nodes.name: Transaction History Route
nodes.description: GET /transactions loads the caller's account and exposes the ledger list as ${transactions} for the statement template.

nodes.name: Principal Lookup
nodes.description: Every authenticated handler repeats the same SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication().getName() lookup followed by findAccountByUsername — the app's de facto current-user resolution.

nodes.name: Web View Layer
nodes.description: Four server-rendered Thymeleaf pages styled as a Wells Fargo retail-banking UI with Bootstrap 4 from a CDN and inline CSS; there is no JavaScript build or SPA.

nodes.name: Dashboard Page
nodes.description: Shows the welcome banner, current balance and account number, and hosts the three POST forms for deposit, withdrawal, and transfer.

nodes.name: Login Page
nodes.description: Public form posting to /login, with a th:if block that renders the bad-credentials alert when ${param.error} is present and a link across to registration.

nodes.name: Registration Page
nodes.description: Public sign-up form posting username and password to /register and rendering the duplicate-username error returned by the service.

nodes.name: Branding & Static Assets
nodes.description: Shared navbar, footer, and the self-hosted Wells Fargo logo served from src/main/resources/static that give all four pages a consistent retail-bank identity.

nodes.name: Template Engine Wiring
nodes.description: Thymeleaf plus the Spring Security 6 dialect are pulled in as starters so controller view names resolve to templates/*.html and security expressions are available in markup.

nodes.name: Application Bootstrap & Configuration
nodes.description: Spring Boot 3.3.3 entrypoint plus the externalisable configuration that binds the app to its MySQL datasource and Hibernate settings at startup.

nodes.name: Spring Boot Entrypoint
nodes.description: @SpringBootApplication class whose main() boots the embedded Tomcat on port 8080; it is also the ENTRYPOINT target of the runtime container image.

nodes.name: Runtime Properties
nodes.description: application.properties hardcodes the local datasource URL, root user, and password; deployments override them with SPRING_DATASOURCE_* environment variables instead of editing the file.

nodes.name: Test Harness
nodes.description: A single @SpringBootTest contextLoads smoke test; because no H2/test profile exists it needs a reachable MySQL to pass, which is why CI builds the image with -DskipTests.

nodes.name: Build & Dependency Management
nodes.description: Maven build inheriting spring-boot-starter-parent 3.3.3, driven through the checked-in Maven Wrapper so builds are reproducible without a local Maven install.

nodes.name: POM & Dependencies
nodes.description: Declares the data-jpa, security, thymeleaf, and web starters, MySQL Connector/J, and the test starters; note java.version is 17 while maven-compiler-plugin is pinned to source/target 1.8.

nodes.name: Maven Wrapper
nodes.description: POSIX and Windows wrapper scripts plus the properties file that pins Apache Maven 3.9.7, used by both local development and the Docker build stage.

nodes.name: Workspace Hygiene
nodes.description: gitignore rules excluding target/, IDE metadata (IntelliJ, STS, NetBeans, VS Code) and build output so only sources and deployment manifests are tracked.

nodes.name: Container & Local Orchestration
nodes.description: Two-stage Docker build producing a slim JRE image, and a Compose stack that runs that image next to MySQL for a one-command local environment.

nodes.name: Multi-stage Image Build
nodes.description: Stage 1 builds the fat jar with maven:3.8.3-openjdk-17 and -DskipTests; stage 2 copies only the jar into openjdk:17-alpine, exposes 8080, and runs it via java -jar.

nodes.name: Compose Stack
nodes.description: Brings up mysql (with a named volume and mysqladmin healthcheck) and the app container, which waits on service_healthy and reaches the DB over the bankapp bridge network using BankDB and allowPublicKeyRetrieval.

nodes.name: Image Coordinates
nodes.description: The .env file supplies DUSER/IMAGE, which Compose interpolates into ${DUSER}/${IMAGE} to select which published Docker Hub image the local stack runs.

nodes.name: Kubernetes Deployment Manifests
nodes.description: Raw manifests for running the app on EKS: a two-replica app Deployment, a single-replica MySQL with hostPath-backed storage, services, autoscaling, and a TLS ingress fronted by cert-manager.

nodes.name: Application Workload
nodes.description: bankapp-deploy runs 2 replicas of trainwithshubham/bankapp-eks:v2 with CPU/memory requests and limits; the health probes are present but commented out.

nodes.name: Database Workload
nodes.description: MySQL 8.0 Deployment mounting the mysql-pvc claim at /var/lib/mysql, with root password from the secret and database name from the ConfigMap.

nodes.name: Cluster Networking
nodes.description: ClusterIP services for the app (8080) and MySQL (3306) inside bankapp-namespace; the MySQL service DNS name is what the ConfigMap's JDBC URL points at.

nodes.name: Persistent Storage
nodes.description: A 10Gi hostPath PersistentVolume with Retain reclaim policy and the matching ReadWriteOnce claim that keeps MySQL data across pod restarts.

nodes.name: Horizontal Autoscaling
nodes.description: HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaling bankapp-deploy between 1 and 5 replicas at 40% average CPU utilisation.

nodes.name: Ingress & TLS Termination
nodes.description: NGINX ingress for megaproject.trainwithshubham.com forcing HTTPS, plus the Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer that cert-manager uses to mint bankapp-tls-secret via HTTP-01.

nodes.name: Cluster Config & Secrets
nodes.description: ConfigMap holding MYSQL_DATABASE and the cluster-internal SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL, and a base64 Secret with the MySQL root and datasource passwords checked into the repo.

nodes.name: Helm Chart Packaging
nodes.description: A parameterised Helm chart that renders the same topology as the raw manifests, but with MySQL as a StatefulSet behind a headless service and every image, port, and resource value driven from values.yaml.

nodes.name: Chart Values
nodes.description: Single source of truth for namespace, image coordinates, NodePort 30080, resource requests/limits, HPA bounds, and the MySQL credentials that the secret template base64-encodes.

nodes.name: Application Templates
nodes.description: Templated Deployment with a busybox initContainer that blocks on the MySQL headless service, actuator liveness/readiness probes, and the NodePort service that exposes the app on 30080.

nodes.name: Database Templates
nodes.description: MySQL StatefulSet with a stable pod identity, its headless service, and the manual-storageClass PV/PVC pair the statefulset mounts.

nodes.name: Scaling Templates
nodes.description: Both a HorizontalPodAutoscaler driven by values.hpa and a VerticalPodAutoscaler in Auto update mode targeting the same Deployment.

nodes.name: Config & Secret Templates
nodes.description: ConfigMap that assembles the fully-qualified StatefulSet JDBC URL from values, and a Secret template that b64enc-encodes the MySQL passwords at render time.

nodes.name: Release UX
nodes.description: Post-install NOTES telling the operator which NodePort URL to open, the optional ingress template, and the chart README with install steps.

nodes.name: CI/CD Pipeline
nodes.description: Two Jenkins declarative pipelines — a CI job that scans, analyses, builds, and pushes the image, and a downstream GitOps CD job that rewrites the Kubernetes image tag and pushes it back to Git.

nodes.name: CI Build Job
nodes.description: Cleans the workspace, checks out the DevOps branch, runs the security and quality gates, builds and pushes the tagged image, then triggers the BankApp-CD job with the same DOCKER_TAG.

nodes.name: GitOps Deploy Job
nodes.description: Receives DOCKER_TAG, seds the new image tag into the Kubernetes deployment manifest, and commits and pushes the change so an ArgoCD sync rolls it out.

nodes.name: Jenkins Shared Library
nodes.description: The vars/ global-variable steps loaded via @Library('Shared'); each groovy file defines one reusable call() step consumed by the two Jenkinsfiles.

nodes.name: Docker Pipeline Steps
nodes.description: Shared steps that build, tag, push (with the dockerhub credentials binding), and clean up images — note the duplicated pairs docker_build/buildImage and docker_push/pushImage.

nodes.name: Compose Deploy Steps
nodes.description: deploy() validates the Compose file, tears the stack down gracefully, brings it back up, and polls docker compose ps until every service reports healthy; docker_compose() is the blunt down/up variant.

nodes.name: Security & Quality Gates
nodes.description: Trivy filesystem scan, OWASP Dependency-Check with report publishing, and SonarQube analysis plus a non-blocking quality gate wait — the DevSecOps checkpoints of the CI job.

nodes.name: Build Notifications
nodes.description: The CD job's post-always emailext block sends an HTML summary with job name, build number, and build URL, attaching the log on every outcome.

nodes.name: Operations Documentation
nodes.description: The runbooks that make this repo a DevSecOps teaching project: EKS/ArgoCD walkthroughs, Jenkins pipeline setup, nginx TLS termination, and ingress configuration, illustrated with screenshots.

nodes.name: Deployment Runbooks
nodes.description: End-to-end AWS EKS deployment guide and its Kubernetes-only variant, covering prerequisites, cluster creation, and Prometheus/Grafana monitoring via Helm.

nodes.name: CI/CD Setup Guide
nodes.description: Describes the CICD workflow and how to wire up the Jenkins jobs, credentials, and shared library that the two Jenkinsfiles assume.

nodes.name: Edge & TLS Guides
nodes.description: How to put nginx in front of the app on EC2 with domain mapping and SSL, and how to install and use the NGINX ingress controller in-cluster.

nodes.name: ArgoCD & Cluster Guide
nodes.description: Step-by-step EKS + ArgoCD setup that closes the GitOps loop: the CD job pushes a manifest change and ArgoCD syncs it to the cluster.

nodes.name: Documentation Screenshots
nodes.description: Reference captures of the application UI and Jenkins agent/flow used throughout the runbooks.
